direction: Light field atlas: paper ground, dark blue-green ink, teal DNA, coral RNA, ochre recognition landmarks; Source Sans 3 and open annotated drawings.
thesis: Cas9 uses an RNA guide and an adjacent PAM to locate DNA; cellular repair determines the edit after cleavage.
model: Local strand separation and RNA–DNA pairing
Alternative end-joining and template-directed repair outcomes
visible_evidence: Large strand-level cutaway inside a schematic Cas9 envelope
DNA and RNA have distinct labelled backbones
PAM sits adjacent to the paired region
A broken duplex branches into directly comparable repair outcomes
Insertion, deletion and templated change are visible in the DNA geometry
reading_order: Molecular recognition at the top, cleavage and repair fork below, then limits on interpretation.
production_contract: Editable vector scene generated by scripts/gallery/crispr.js. Molecular geometry and sequence blocks are original conceptual drawings.
scope: Conventional double-strand-cutting Cas9, not base or prime editing. No actual target sequence, molecular scale, protocol or outcome frequency. Repair pathways are simplified and not exhaustive.
